title: The Two Tables: Cadman Plaza, 800 Third Avenue, and the Trial of the Decade
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Ithaca, Ann Arbor, and the Sacred Sites Note

stops.name: Cornell University, the Phi Beta Kappa key
stops.date_confidence: Year attested by the firm biography; the June date is a placement for commencement. Birth is given as January 1963, month and year only, by the United Kingdom Companies House register for Cohen & Gresser (UK) LLP; no day, and no birthplace, appears in any reachable source. An earlier reconstruction giving 1962 is superseded by the filing.
stops.campa: He takes a bachelor's degree at Cornell and is elected to Phi Beta Kappa, and that is very nearly everything the public record holds about the first twenty-one years of his life. A British company filing four decades later will give January 1963 as the month of his birth, and no day. The firm biography that reports the degree does not say what he took it in. No source names the town he was born in, the school he attended before this one, or the family that sent him up to this hill above Cayuga Lake.
sources: UK Companies House PSC register, Cohen & Gresser (UK) LLP, OC421038
suggested_refs: Cornell University commencement records, class of 1984

stops.name: Hutchins Hall, the review of Judge Hastie
stops.date_confidence: Volume year attested by the Michigan Law Review's own issue page; no month is recorded, and the date defaults to January.
stops.campa: In his second year at Michigan he publishes a review in the Law Review under the title William Hastie: Grace Under Pressure, on the civil rights lawyer who became the first Black judge to sit on a United States court of appeals. It is a young man's piece about a career spent arguing inside a system that did not want the argument. He is twenty-three years old and has never seen the inside of a federal trial. The piece runs at 84 Michigan Law Review 861.
sources: Michigan Law Review, volume 84 issue page, University of Michigan Law School repository
suggested_refs: Mark S. Cohen, 'William Hastie: Grace Under Pressure,' 84 Mich. L. Rev. 861 (1986)

stops.name: Hutchins Hall, the note on the sacred sites
stops.date_confidence: Volume year attested by the University of Michigan Law School repository; no month recorded, date defaults to January. The note is his own work in his own year and carries no forward reference of any kind.
stops.campa: His student note runs at 85 Michigan Law Review 771, under the title American Indian Sacred Religious Sites and Government Development: A Conventional Analysis in an Unconventional Setting. The argument is that courts have mishandled ordinary Free Exercise analysis when the thing to be protected is a mountain or a burial ground rather than a congregation, and that the doctrine needs restructuring to see it. He proposes a test. It is the only sustained constitutional scholarship he will publish, and he is a Note Editor of the Law Review the same year.
sources: University of Michigan Law School repository, 85 Mich. L. Rev. 771 (1987)
suggested_refs: Mark S. Cohen, 'American Indian Sacred Religious Sites and Government Development,' 85 Mich. L. Rev. 771 (1987)

stops.name: Ann Arbor, the degree magna cum laude
stops.date_confidence: Degree and honours attested by the firm biography; the May date is a placement for the graduation month, which no source gives.
stops.campa: He takes the J.D. magna cum laude and leaves Ann Arbor for New York with a Law Review masthead line and no clients. A year ahead of him in the same building is Lawrence T. Gresser, class of 1986, whom he has not yet had reason to notice. Thirty-one years from now the two of them will put a hundred thousand dollars into a scholarship fund at this law school carrying both their names, by which time the name will belong to a firm with offices on three continents. In May of 1987 it belongs to nobody.
sources: Michigan Law Quadrangle, Spring/Summer 2018, on the Cohen & Gresser Scholarship Fund
suggested_refs: University of Michigan Law School, class of 1987 records
The Cohen & Gresser Scholarship Fund, endowed 2018

stops.name: One New York Plaza, the associate at Fried Frank
stops.date_confidence: SEQUENCING UNRESOLVED AND FLAGGED. The firm biography states he practised at Fried Frank before founding Cohen & Gresser and attaches no years to it. One reading of the pool put this before his federal service, one after, one on both sides. The dossier states outright that the sources do not settle it. 1987 is a placement, not a finding. The address is the firm's New York office of the era.
stops.campa: He begins in private practice at Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver and Jacobson, in the tower at the foot of Manhattan where the firm keeps its New York office. His own biography, written decades later, lists the job with no years attached to it, and no reachable source settles whether this comes before his years as a federal prosecutor, after them, or on both sides. What is certain is that the first building of his working life is a corporate one, at the foot of Broad Street by the harbour, and that he does not stay in it very long.
sources: OpenStreetMap, One New York Plaza, 1 Water Street
suggested_refs: Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson, New York office, One New York Plaza

stops.name: 271 Cadman Plaza East, the Assistant United States Attorney
stops.date_confidence: RECONSTRUCTION. No primary personnel record for the appointment was located. The hard anchors are a federal opinion of 27 March 1995 naming him as an AUSA and a Second Circuit opinion of 1996 calling him a former one. 1990 is a reconstruction; a competing reconstruction gave c. 1988, which the 1995 opinion does not disturb but does not support either.
stops.campa: He crosses the river and takes the government's side. The United States Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York sits on Cadman Plaza in Brooklyn, and its assistants try narcotics, racketeering, and organised crime across Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island, and Long Island. He conducts numerous jury trials out of this office. The day he was sworn in is on no page that can now be reached; what can be reached is a federal opinion of March 1995 that names him as an assistant, and another of 1996 that calls him a former one.
sources: United States v. Gangi, 27 March 1995, via CaseMine
suggested_refs: United States Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York, 271 Cadman Plaza East

stops.name: 225 Cadman Plaza East, the seven weeks of United States v. Pitera
stops.date_confidence: Trial year attested; the May date is a placement counted back seven weeks from the 25 June 1992 conviction. NOTE ON THE BUILDING: in 1992 the EDNY sat in the six-storey Emanuel Celler Federal Building on this site. The Theodore Roosevelt Courthouse now standing here did not open until 2006 and must not be named for this stop.
stops.campa: The defendant is Thomas Pitera, a Bonanno family soldier and contract killer, and the case is among the first brought in New York under the death penalty provisions of the Anti-Drug Abuse Act. The trial runs seven weeks in the Emanuel Celler Federal Building, the squat six-storey courthouse standing on Cadman Plaza in 1992; the courthouse that replaces it will not open for another fourteen years. Cohen is a junior prosecutor on the team, and the firm biography claims no more for him than that. He is twenty-nine years old.
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Theodore Roosevelt United States Courthouse'
suggested_refs: United States v. Pitera, E.D.N.Y., trial record 1992

stops.name: 225 Cadman Plaza East, Pitera convicted
stops.date_confidence: Date attested by English Wikipedia, 'Thomas Pitera'.
stops.campa: The jury convicts. Pitera goes to prison for life; no death sentence is returned. For a prosecutor not yet thirty it is the result that fixes a career, a seven-week federal jury trial against organised crime, won, with his name on the government's side of the caption. Thirty-one years and four miles will separate this verdict from the one he hears read at the other table, in another building, with three cooperating insiders having testified against his own client. Both juries take the government's account of what happened.
suggested_refs: United States v. Pitera, E.D.N.Y., verdict of 25 June 1992

stops.name: 225 Cadman Plaza East, the record of leaving
stops.date_confidence: The 27 March 1995 opinion is attested and is the hardest documentary proof of his service anywhere reachable. The departure is dated only by a 1996 Second Circuit opinion calling him a former assistant; no day is recoverable, and the years 1996 to 2002 are not documented at all.
stops.campa: A federal decision issued on the twenty-seventh of March names Mark Cohen and Elisa Liang as Assistant United States Attorneys for the Eastern District of New York. It is a routine ruling in a routine case and it is the hardest proof of his prosecutorial service that survives in any reachable archive. By the following year a Second Circuit panel is calling him Former AUSA Cohen. Between those two sentences he leaves the government. Where he practises from 1996 to 2002, and on what, is recorded on no page that can be reached.
sources: United States v. Gangi, 27 March 1995, via CaseMine
suggested_refs: United States v. Gangi, E.D.N.Y., opinion of 27 March 1995

stops.name: 800 Third Avenue, the firm founded with Gresser
stops.date_confidence: Founding year and founders attested by Wikipedia's 'Cohen & Gresser' entry and by the firm's own New York office history page; no founding month or day is published, and the date defaults to January.
stops.campa: With Lawrence Gresser, a year ahead of him at Michigan Law, he founds Cohen & Gresser in New York. The two of them are the whole of it. He takes the managing partnership of the New York office and holds it for the next quarter century, while the firm puts down offices in Paris in 2014, Washington in 2016, London in 2018, and Dubai in 2025. The address that becomes the fixed point of the rest of his life is 800 Third Avenue in Turtle Bay, forty blocks north of every courthouse he works in.
sources: Cohen & Gresser LLP, New York office history page
Cohen & Gresser LLP, corporate practice history page
suggested_refs: Cohen & Gresser LLP, founding records, New York, 2002

stops.name: 800 Third Avenue, the first deposition
stops.date_confidence: Publication date attested by the firm biography's own publications list (1 April 2005).
stops.campa: On the first of April he publishes a short piece for young lawyers called The First Deposition: Themes and Variations, and it opens a practitioner bibliography that will run in the firm's own list for the next twenty years. Antitrust liability as the stakes get higher. Insider trading in debt securities. The Foreign Corrupt Practices Act in the whistleblower era. Failed banks and the insiders the FDIC comes after. Federal sentencing under the amended economic crimes guideline. The extraterritorial reach of the Sherman Act.
sources: Cohen & Gresser LLP attorney biography, publications list
suggested_refs: Mark S. Cohen, 'The First Deposition: Themes and Variations' (2005)

stops.name: 800 Third Avenue, the case against JPMorgan Chase
stops.date_confidence: The litigation is attested by the reported decision in JP Morgan Chase Bank v. Coleman-Toll; the 2008 to 2009 window comes from the dossier, and January 2009 is a placement inside it. PIN: his own office, not Nevada. No source places him personally in Henderson or Las Vegas, and a stop belongs to whoever was actually there.
stops.campa: He appears for Meritage Homes of Nevada in litigation brought by JPMorgan Chase and a syndicate of lenders out of the collapse of Inspirada, a planned development at Henderson, Nevada. The New York proceedings are transferred west. This is the plainest documented contact between Cohen and that bank, and it runs the opposite way from the one people later assume: he is not its lawyer, he is across the table from it. Eight years afterward his firm will hire a man who spent fourteen years as a JPMorgan managing director and associate general counsel.
sources: JP Morgan Chase Bank, N.A. v. Coleman-Toll Limited Partnership, via CaseMine
Cohen & Gresser LLP news release, 18 April 2017, on the hiring of Kwaku Andoh
suggested_refs: JP Morgan Chase Bank v. Coleman-Toll Ltd. P'ship, S.D.N.Y. and D. Nev.

stops.name: 800 Third Avenue, the client retained in 2009
stops.date_confidence: The year is attested by the 2016 privilege opinion in Giuffre v. Maxwell, which recites Maxwell's declaration that she retained Brett Jaffe of Cohen & Gresser in 2009 and that Cohen continued as her United States counsel after Jaffe left. No month is given anywhere; June is a placement. No source establishes that Jeffrey Epstein ever retained Cohen or this firm.
stops.campa: A client comes to the firm this year and does not leave. Ghislaine Maxwell retains Brett Jaffe of Cohen & Gresser for United States legal matters and a deposition, and when Jaffe departs the firm Cohen continues as her American counsel. The retention falls in the long quiet interval after Jeffrey Epstein's Florida plea, when the matters touching her are civil and the depositions are sealed. None of it appears on a public page for another seven years, and nothing reachable establishes that Epstein ever retained Cohen or this firm.
sources: Giuffre v. Maxwell, S.D.N.Y., privilege opinion of 2016, via Justia
suggested_refs: Giuffre v. Maxwell, S.D.N.Y. 15-cv-7433, privilege opinion documenting the 2009 retention

stops.name: 225 Cadman Plaza East, monitor of the Fire Department
stops.date_confidence: Appointment attested; firm materials date it to November 2011 and Judge Garaufis's monitorship order is recorded for 2011. The END date is a gap: the firm describes the role as running about a decade and gives no closing year. An earlier reading dating the role c. 2013 to 2018 is wrong at both ends.
stops.campa: Judge Nicholas Garaufis, having found the city's firefighter hiring discriminatory, orders a monitor placed over the Fire Department of New York, and the Eastern District appoints Cohen to the post. It is not a client relationship and there is nobody for him to defend. He reports to the court on whether the largest fire department in the country is doing what it has been ordered to do about who it hires and who it keeps, and he holds the role for roughly a decade. The underlying litigation settles for ninety-eight million dollars.
suggested_refs: United States v. City of New York, E.D.N.Y., FDNY hiring monitorship, 2011 onward

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the complete defence verdict
stops.date_confidence: Date attested by the dossier as the day of the verdict for Peter Black. VENUE IS A RECONSTRUCTION: the firm biography never names the courthouse, and the related SEC proceeding was a Southern District case, so 500 Pearl Street is inference and is flagged as such. The pin is the atlas's canonical figure for this building.
stops.campa: He tries a two-week jury case for Peter Black, a former Wynnefield Capital analyst charged by the Securities and Exchange Commission with insider trading, and the jury clears his client on everything. AmLaw's Litigation Daily names him Litigator of the Week. He is fifty-one, twenty-two years past Pitera, and he now knows the shape of a federal courtroom from both tables in it. Four years later he and the same colleague will get an SEC complaint against a former Och-Ziff analyst dismissed outright, and the Commission will not appeal.
suggested_refs: SEC v. Obus, S.D.N.Y., jury verdict of 30 May 2014

stops.name: Universite Paris I Pantheon-Sorbonne, the white-collar course
stops.date_confidence: The teaching is attested but undated in the firm biography, which describes it as long-running. The Paris office opening in 2014 is separately attested and the stop is placed at the start of the academic year following it; September 2014 is a placement, not a record. The only year with a named course and named co-teachers is 2017, which is stated in the campa.
stops.campa: Cohen & Gresser opens in Paris this year, and he begins teaching United States white-collar criminal law to French law students at the Universite Paris I Pantheon-Sorbonne on the rue des Ecoles. What he brings into the lecture hall is procedure rather than doctrine: how an American prosecutor assembles a financial case out of records and cooperators. By 2017 the course carries that title outright, taught with Muriel Goldberg-Darmon, with his colleagues Christian Everdell and Jonathan Abernethy coming in as visiting lecturers. He never moves to France.
suggested_refs: Universite Paris I Pantheon-Sorbonne, course 'U.S. White Collar Criminal Law', 2017

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the name in the privilege ruling
stops.date_confidence: The opinion is dated to 2016 with no day recoverable here. 22 April 2016 is the date of the Maxwell deposition entered on the same docket and is used to order the segment. Cohen's continuation as United States counsel is the court's recital of the client's own declaration, supported by an email the court found consistent with it.
stops.campa: A federal judge rules on privilege in Giuffre v. Maxwell, the civil defamation suit, and the opinion recites what Ghislaine Maxwell has declared about her own lawyers: that she hired Brett Jaffe of Cohen & Gresser in 2009, and that after Jaffe left the firm Mark Cohen continued as her United States counsel while Philip Barden acted for her in England. The court finds an email consistent with her account. It is the first time the relationship appears on a public page anywhere. The suit settles under seal the following June.
sources: Giuffre v. Maxwell, S.D.N.Y., privilege opinion of 2016, via Justia
suggested_refs: Giuffre v. Maxwell, S.D.N.Y. 15-cv-7433, docket entry 135

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the appearance entered
stops.date_confidence: The arrest of 2 July 2020 and the bail refusal of 14 July 2020 are attested. The docket records Mark Stewart Cohen entering an appearance shortly after the arrest; no source gives the exact filing day, so the stop is dated to the bail hearing.
stops.campa: Maxwell is arrested in New Hampshire on the second of July and brought to the Southern District. Cohen, who has handled her American civil matters for eleven quiet years, enters his appearance as counsel of record in a federal sex trafficking prosecution, on a docket the whole world is reading line by line. At the hearing on the fourteenth the government opposes any release at all. The court refuses bail, and she is taken to the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, where she will be held through the trial and through the sentence.
sources: CourtListener docket, United States v. Maxwell
United States Department of Justice, Maxwell case page
suggested_refs: United States v. Maxwell, S.D.N.Y. 20-cr-330, notice of appearance

stops.name: 800 Third Avenue, the letter listing JPMorgan Chase materials
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date on the document itself: a Department of Justice discovery letter of 2 February 2021 addressed in part to Christian Everdell and Mark Cohen at Cohen & Gresser. The stop is pinned at the office the letter was addressed to.
stops.campa: A discovery letter goes out from the United States Attorney's Office addressed to Christian Everdell and Mark Cohen at Cohen & Gresser, and its production index carries a line reading REPRODUCTION, JPMorgan Chase materials, some seven hundred and ninety-four pages of them. Bank records enter the defence file. Nothing reachable says Cohen ever represented that bank, held an account with it, was paid by it, or knew what its compliance officers had written about his client ten years earlier. The letter says what it says and no more.
sources: Department of Justice discovery letter, 2 February 2021, EFTA00011267, rollcall.com Epstein files production
suggested_refs: DOJ production letter of 2 February 2021, United States v. Maxwell

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the Maxwell trial opens
stops.date_confidence: Trial opening date attested. Cohen's role is stated in the firm's own careful words and is NOT the same as lead trial counsel; the courtroom team is separately named. Press shorthand calling him her lawyer, singular, is an oversimplification and is flagged rather than repeated.
stops.campa: The trial opens before Judge Alison Nathan. Cohen's own firm describes his part precisely and modestly: he handled the initial proceedings and served as strategic adviser to the trial team. The lawyers who carry the courtroom are Bobbi Sternheim, Christian Everdell, Laura Menninger, and Jeffrey Pagliuca. He has been inside this client's legal affairs longer than any of them and he is not the one on his feet. The press calls him her lawyer, in the singular, and that is the shorthand that sticks.
suggested_refs: United States v. Maxwell, S.D.N.Y., trial transcript, 29 November to 29 December 2021

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the verdict on five counts
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Department of Justice announcement: conviction on five of six counts after a month-long trial.
stops.campa: After a month of testimony the jury convicts on five counts of six. It is a defeat, and the firm biography keeps the matter listed anyway, under its own heading, among the leading jury trials of the practice. A criminal defence record is a record of other people's convictions as often as it is anything else; the work is measured against what the sentence would otherwise have been, and that quantity is never published anywhere. He will be back in this building inside a year, for a different client, in a case that gets four times the coverage.
sources: United States Department of Justice, Maxwell sentencing announcement
suggested_refs: United States v. Maxwell, S.D.N.Y., verdict of 29 December 2021

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the twenty-year sentence
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date, from the Department of Justice sentencing announcement: 240 months, five years supervised release, a fine of 750,000 dollars.
stops.campa: Judge Nathan imposes two hundred and forty months, twenty years, with five years of supervised release and a fine of seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars. The client Cohen picked up in 2009 as a civil matter goes to federal prison for two decades. Five months later and four thousand miles south of here a cryptocurrency exchange collapses inside a week, and a young man in the Bahamas with no criminal lawyer starts looking for one. The lawyer he will find is standing in this courtroom on the twenty-eighth of June, watching his own client sentenced.
sources: United States Department of Justice, sentencing announcement of 28 June 2022
suggested_refs: United States v. Maxwell, S.D.N.Y., judgment of 28 June 2022

stops.name: 800 Third Avenue, the retention reported
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date: Reuters, 6 December 2022. The date the retainer was actually signed is not on any reachable page; the report is the anchor.
stops.campa: Reuters reports that Sam Bankman-Fried, whose exchange failed in November and whose previous firm has withdrawn citing conflicts, has hired Mark S. Cohen of Cohen & Gresser. The client is still in the Bahamas and has not yet been arrested. Christian Everdell, who worked the Maxwell defence beside Cohen, comes on as principal co-counsel, so the same two lawyers in the same order take the second of the two most photographed federal defendants of the decade. Six days later Bahamian police arrest their client at his apartment in Nassau.
suggested_refs: Reuters report of 6 December 2022 on the retention of Cohen & Gresser

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the extradition and the bond
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date: extradited to the United States and released on a 250 million dollar bond secured against his parents' Palo Alto home. A reading that placed the argument for this bond in February 2023 conflated it with the later fights over tightening bail conditions and is corrected here.
stops.campa: Bankman-Fried is flown to New York and appears in the Southern District. The court sets a bond of two hundred and fifty million dollars, secured against his parents' house in Palo Alto. It is the largest pretrial bond ever written in an American criminal case, and it is a defence result: the government's fraud defendant walks out of the building on the day he arrives in the country. Almost everything Cohen wins in this case he wins in the nine months before the trial. His client goes west that week, into his parents' custody in California.
suggested_refs: United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y. 22-cr-673, bail order of 22 December 2022

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the plea of not guilty
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date: he pleaded not guilty on 3 January 2023. An earlier reading folded this into the 22 December extradition; the two events are twelve days apart and are kept apart here.
stops.campa: He stands with his client at the arraignment and Bankman-Fried pleads not guilty to eight counts of fraud and conspiracy. Judge Lewis A. Kaplan, seventy-eight years old and thirty years on this bench, has the case. A trial date is set for October. The defendant will spend the intervening months on his parents' property in Palo Alto with a laptop, writing to journalists and to former colleagues, which is eventually how the bail is lost. None of that is visible from the well of the court on the third of January.
suggested_refs: United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y., arraignment of 3 January 2023

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the counts severed
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date: Reuters, 15 June 2023. The firm describes the outcome as the removal of six charges; the procedural record shows five counts severed and held for a March 2024 trial that never took place. Both framings are recorded and neither is resolved into the other.
stops.campa: The defence argues that counts added after extradition cannot be tried without the consent of the Bahamas, invoking the doctrine of specialty, and prosecutors agree to sever them and hold them for a second trial in March. It is the most technical and most successful piece of lawyering Cohen does in this case. His firm will later describe it as the removal of six charges. What actually happens is that they are set aside, and after the first verdict the government simply declines to bring them back.
suggested_refs: United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y., severance order of June 2023

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the bail revoked
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date: Judge Kaplan revoked the bond on 11 August 2023 over witness tampering allegations and ordered him detained pending trial.
stops.campa: Judge Kaplan finds that the defendant has been contacting witnesses, including by giving a reporter the private writings of a former colleague, and revokes the bond. Bankman-Fried is remanded from the courtroom and driven across the river. Cohen loses the two hundred and fifty million dollar release he obtained in December. From here to the verdict his client sleeps in Brooklyn and is bussed across the river for hearings, working on his own defence from a jail laptop whose internet connection barely functions. Trial is eight weeks away.
suggested_refs: United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y., bail revocation of 11 August 2023

stops.name: Metropolitan Detention Center, Brooklyn, the visiting room
stops.date_confidence: RECONSTRUCTION. The detention from 11 August 2023 is attested; no source reachable places Cohen personally inside this building on any particular day. The stop is carried as inference from the requirements of preparing a five-week trial with a detained client, and the 15 August date orders the segment rather than recording an event. Pin inherited byte-identical from the atlas.
stops.campa: The federal jail on Twenty-ninth Street in Sunset Park has a documented history of lockdowns, power failures, and defence lawyers turned away at the door. Bankman-Fried is held here for the eight weeks before trial and throughout it. No reachable source puts Cohen in the visiting rooms on any given day, and this stop is inference: a lead trial lawyer with a detained client and a five-week fraud trial coming has nowhere else to build it. The client he defended before this one was held in the same building for two years.
suggested_refs: Metropolitan Detention Center, Brooklyn, 80 29th Street, attorney visitation records (not public)

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the jury chosen
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date: jury selection opened on 3 October 2023. An earlier reading placed the opening statements on this day as well; they were the following day.
stops.campa: Jury selection in United States v. Samuel Bankman-Fried. Kaplan questions the panel himself and seats twelve jurors and six alternates inside a single day, faster than either side expects. For the government it is Nicolas Roos and Danielle Sassoon, out of the same federal prosecutor's service Cohen belonged to on the other side of the river. More than sixty news organisations are credentialed. The defence table is Cohen, Everdell, and a defendant in a suit that no longer fits him. Openings are tomorrow.
suggested_refs: United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y., voir dire transcript, 3 October 2023

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the opening statement
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date: opening statements were delivered 4 October 2023 (Time, 5 October 2023, which quotes the 'math nerd' line from that day). An earlier reading dated this to 3 October, which was jury selection.
stops.campa: Cohen opens for the defence. He tells the jury his client is a math nerd who did not drink or party, a hard-working entrepreneur who got in over his head, and that Bankman-Fried reasonably believed nothing in the exchange's terms of service forbade lending out customer deposits. The theory is that the money was permitted to move and the risk management was bad. Bad risk management is not a federal crime. The government has just spent an hour describing a theft, and the jury has heard that version first.
stops.quote: It's not a crime to be the CEO of a company that later files for bankruptcy.
stops.quote_source: Mark Cohen, opening statement, United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y., 4 October 2023
sources: Time, 'The 3 Key Battle Lines in Sam Bankman-Fried's Trial', 5 October 2023
suggested_refs: United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y., opening statement transcript, 4 October 2023

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, Caroline Ellison cross-examined
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Ellison testified from 10 October and the cross-examination continued on 11 October. Nishad Singh testified on 16 October; Gary Wang also cooperated. The characterisation of how the cross went is contested professional opinion, not a finding, and is presented as a disagreement.
stops.campa: Caroline Ellison, who ran Alameda Research and has already pleaded guilty, testifies that Bankman-Fried directed her to commit crimes, and the defence cross-examines her across two days. Commentators watching say the defence is landing nothing; defence lawyers reading the same transcript say there was nothing available to land against three insiders holding signed plea agreements. She is the government's central witness and she does not come apart. Gary Wang and Nishad Singh, both co-founders, both cooperating, testify in the same weeks.
sources: WIRED, 'Sam Bankman-Fried's Lawyers Are Doing Just Fine, Actually'
suggested_refs: United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y., trial transcript, 10 to 11 October 2023

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the hearing outside the jury's presence
stops.date_confidence: Attested: on 26 October 2023 Bankman-Fried testified outside the jury's presence in an admissibility hearing. An earlier reading treated this as the opening of the defence case with a single witness; the defence in fact called three.
stops.campa: Kaplan sends the jury out and hears the defendant testify about what he intends to say, so the court can rule in advance on how much of it the jury may hear. It is an unusual procedure and not a good sign. The judge admits some of the advice-of-counsel material and keeps most of it out. The defence has two other witnesses, Krystal Rolle, a Bahamian attorney, and Joseph Pimbley, a risk-management expert, and neither of them can say the thing that only the defendant can say.
suggested_refs: United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y., admissibility hearing transcript, 26 October 2023

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the direct examination
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Bankman-Fried's testimony before the jury began 27 October 2023, questioned by his own trial team led by Cohen.
stops.campa: Bankman-Fried takes the stand in front of the jury and Cohen questions him: the founding of Alameda, the founding of FTX, the terms of service, the borrowing, the week the whole thing came down. It is the entire defence case and it rests on twelve people believing a young man who has spent a year explaining himself in public to anyone who asked. He is fluent on direct. Kaplan interrupts repeatedly on form. The examination runs into a second day and finishes on the morning of the thirtieth. Then the government stands up.

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the cross-examination opens
stops.date_confidence: Attested: cross-examination BEGAN on 30 October 2023. An earlier reading said it continued that day, which reverses the order of the trial's last week.
stops.campa: Danielle Sassoon begins the cross-examination and the fluency stops. Asked what he told investors, what he told customers, what he told his own employees, the defendant answers that he does not recall, or that it depends what is meant, well over a hundred times by the count of reporters in the room. The case Cohen built rests on twelve people believing this witness, and Cohen sits at the defence table with nothing to do but listen to him. Kaplan sustains objection after objection to the form of the answers.
sources: WIRED, 'Sam Bankman-Fried's Lawyers Are Doing Just Fine, Actually'

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the defence rests
stops.date_confidence: Attested: cross-examination concluded, redirect followed, and the defence rested on 31 October 2023, with closing arguments set for the following morning.
stops.campa: Cross-examination finishes, Cohen takes his client on redirect, and the defence rests. Three witnesses in all: a Bahamian attorney, a risk-management expert, and the defendant. The government called many more over five weeks, among them three former colleagues who had already pleaded guilty and agreed to cooperate. Closing arguments are set for nine thirty the next morning. Outside, on the last day of October, Foley Square fills with office workers in costume walking past the television trucks.

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the closing argument
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date: closing arguments 1 November 2023. Two earlier readings misdated these lines, one to 26 October and one to the 3 October opening, and attributed them to The Verge and The Guardian. They belong to the closing and were carried by Courthouse News Service, CNN, and Reuters, all 1 November 2023. The line about the real world and the movie world is paraphrased in the campa rather than quoted, because the original punctuates with em dashes.
stops.campa: Cohen closes for the defence. He tells the jury the government has spent five weeks trying to turn Sam into some sort of villain, some sort of monster, and that it is both wrong and unfair; that in the real world, as against the movie world, things get messy, and poor risk management is not a crime; that a criminal mastermind would not have gone in front of Congress and subjected himself to public questioning when he did not have to. Not one witness, he says, testified that anybody was ever told to steal.

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the verdict on all seven counts
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date and approximate hour: the jury retired at about 3:15 in the afternoon and returned guilty on all seven counts in under five hours.
stops.campa: The trial has run five weeks. The jury is charged and retires at about a quarter past three in the afternoon, and it comes back in under five hours with a verdict of guilty on all seven counts. Bankman-Fried stands to hear it read. Cohen stands beside him. Two of his clients have now been convicted by juries in this courthouse inside two years. The statement his defence gives afterward says they respect the jury's decision, that his client maintains his innocence, and that they will continue to vigorously fight the charges.

stops.campa: Prosecutors tell Judge Kaplan they will not try the counts severed in June, citing the public interest in prompt resolution and the fact that the evidence behind them was largely aired at the first trial. The specialty fight Cohen won in the summer ends with those charges never tried at all. On paper it is a defence victory and it goes into the firm's account of the matter as one. It arrives seven weeks after the verdict that made it beside the point.

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the sentence of twenty-five years
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date: 25 years imposed, with forfeiture of roughly eleven billion dollars, per the Department of Justice announcement.
stops.campa: Kaplan sentences Bankman-Fried to twenty-five years in federal prison and orders forfeiture of roughly eleven billion dollars. The judge says on the record that the defendant lied on the witness stand in front of him. Twenty-one months earlier, in this same building on Pearl Street, Cohen stood while another judge of this district sent Ghislaine Maxwell away for twenty years. He is sixty-one years old and has been trying federal cases for more than thirty. The date is the twenty-eighth of March.

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the notice of appeal filed
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date. GEOGRAPHY CORRECTED: an earlier reading staged this at the Thurgood Marshall courthouse 'one block north'. A notice of appeal is filed in the district court at 500 Pearl Street; the appellate courthouse is at 40 Centre Street, across the street. Cohen's role in the appeal itself is a gap and no source reached settles it either way.
stops.campa: The defence files a notice of appeal of the conviction and the sentence. The filing is made in the district court on Pearl Street, which is where a notice of appeal is always made; the Second Circuit sits across the street at 40 Centre Street and does not receive the case for months. Cohen is trial counsel and not appellate counsel, and nothing reachable establishes what part he takes in what follows. A motion for a new trial, alleging bias by the judge, is filed on the thirteenth of September.

stops.name: Harrisburg, the Justice William Strong Lecture
stops.date_confidence: Attested, exact date, from the firm biography. PIN APPROXIMATE: it locates the Widener Commonwealth Law School campus on Vartan Way, Harrisburg; the exact building coordinate was not independently verified.
stops.campa: He delivers the Justice William Strong Lecture at Widener Commonwealth Law School in Harrisburg, on the ethical obligations of prosecutors and of defence lawyers in white-collar cases. He has held both of the jobs he is describing, thirty years apart, and lost the second one in front of sixty news organisations eleven months ago. The lecture becomes an article, written with Sri Kuehnlenz and published the following spring. It is the first thing he has published about the ethics of his own trade.

stops.name: 225 Cadman Plaza East, eight weeks and another conviction
stops.date_confidence: Verdict date attested by the Eastern District's own announcement. Cohen's role as defence counsel in the eight-week trial is firm-reported; the identification of the defendant as Adam Kaplan comes from the Department of Justice announcement.
stops.campa: He is back on Cadman Plaza, at the other table from the office that made him, defending Adam Kaplan in an eight-week federal fraud trial over money taken from advisory clients on Long Island. The prosecutors are the successors of the assistants he sat beside in 1992, working out of a courthouse since torn down and rebuilt on the same plaza. On the thirteenth of November the jury convicts Kaplan and his twin brother Daniel on conspiracy, bank and wire fraud, money laundering, and attempted obstruction.

stops.name: 800 Third Avenue, the record affirmed
stops.date_confidence: The affirmance of 12 June 2026 is attested. The stop is pinned at Cohen's own office rather than at the appellate courthouse, because he was trial counsel and not appellate counsel and no source places him in that courtroom. What the Second Circuit reviewed was the record he made in October and November 2023.
stops.campa: The Second Circuit affirms Bankman-Fried's conviction and his twenty-five-year sentence. Other lawyers argue the appeal. What the court reviews is the record Cohen made across five weeks in the autumn of 2023, and it holds. The firm at 800 Third Avenue is about seventy lawyers now and has been in talks with private equity over a forty-million-dollar convertible note; whether that deal ever closed is on no page anyone has reached. He is sixty-three, and the firm still lists him as managing partner of the New York office and as a lawyer who tries cases.
